output.brief: The jump in write-offs comes mainly from inside the DC, not from Haverlow. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (27 July), chilled pallets wait about 3 h 52 min on an unrefrigerated dock, instead of 44 min. The dock averages 15–17°C overnight. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, Pellridge and own-label included. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open, with no trend. The 6.5–8°C receipt probes are keyed after the long dock wait, so they measure warming on site. The chambers are fine. A chargeback and volume move against Haverlow would punish the wrong party and leave the cause in place. Do not drop the night probe either, because that would hide the problem. Restore night receiving staff, or otherwise cut dock-to-chamber time, and set a maximum time monitored weekly from scan data. Separately, a smaller part of the rise is in customer credits. These roughly doubled after Corriebank's self-certified claims began on 3 August. Whether any claims are inflated is not established. Sample Corriebank's claims against lots before changing credit terms. I'm confident in the main diagnosis. The credit question is still open.
